function: Semi-blind uplink channel estimation: LMMSE estimators using a subspace from pilot and payload symbols, with GMM and VAE learned channel priors (pp. 1, 6-7)
system: Uplink massive MIMO, BS with M=64 antennas (ULA lambda/2 in model; 4x16 URA in measurements), J=8 single-antenna users, no RIS; measurements at 2.18 GHz (pp. 2-3, 9)
method: Semi-blind LMMSE (subspace and projected variants) parameterized by a GMM (EM fit, K=64) or a VAE (ELBO, latent dimension 32), unsupervised offline training on channel samples (pp. 6-9)
data_channel: 3GPP spatial channel model (document 25.996 [35]) and measured data (Nokia campus, Stuttgart, 2.18 GHz); 1.5e5 training samples, 1e3 unseen test samples per model (pp. 3, 9)
test_conditions: Trained and tested separately on each channel model, 1e3 unseen test samples; sweeps over SNR, antennas, snapshots and users; no cross-model or unseen-scenario test (pp. 9-12)
baselines: Non-learned: LS, subspace ML, sample-covariance LMMSE, EM [15], message passing [16]; learned: pilot-only GMM [30] and VAE [32], decision-directed GMM; CRB and BCRB bounds (pp. 9-10)
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, number of antennas, snapshots and users; analytical MSE, CRB and BCRB curves (pp. 5-12)
complexity: Orders given: projected GMM O(KM^2+JM^2), projected VAE O(DM^2+JM^2), subspace calculation O((N+J)M^2), PAST tracking O(JM) (p. 8)
q1_support: p. 3: "we utilize real-world data from a measurement campaign conducted at the Nokia campus in Stuttgart"; p. 9: "training samples from the respective channel model to train the GMM and VAE", so training and testing use measured channels; the other model follows 3GPP document 25.996 [35].
q2_support: p. 9: "unseen channel samples stemming from the channel models detailed in Sections II-A and II-B" - test samples come from the same models used for training; sweeps over SNR, M, J and N (pp. 10-12); no cross-model or unseen-scenario test.
q3_support: p. 9: "we also compare to the pilot-only GMM [30] and VAE [32]" (earlier learned estimators) and "Lastly, we compare our proposed methods to two iterative" algorithms, EM [15] and MP [16], besides LS, ML and sample-covariance LMMSE (non-learned); NMSE in Fig. 4 (p. 10).
q4_support: p. 8: "For the projected versions of the GMM and VAE the complexity becomes" O(KM^2 + JM^2) and O(DM^2 + JM^2), respectively; subspace calculation O((N+J)M^2).
q5_support: p. 3: "we utilize real-world data from a measurement campaign conducted at the Nokia campus in Stuttgart" - trained and tested on measured data (p. 9); no code or data link is given.
notes: Included, area 2: GMM (EM fit) and VAE (ELBO) are learned offline on channel samples and serve as priors of the LMMSE estimators (pp. 6-9). The synthetic model is 3GPP document 25.996 [35], not TR 38.901, flagged for the reviewer; q1 is met anyway through measured data (p. 3). q5 is met only through the measured-data clause: no code or data link is given and the measurements come from the authors' campaign [36] (p. 3). q3: the learned baselines GMM [30] and VAE [32] are earlier published estimators but also the proposed ones without the semi-blind module (p. 9). Title on p. 1 matches the DOI.
